history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Kirti Mandir (lit. 'Temple of Fame') is the royal cenotaph and memorial museum of the Gaekwad dynasty, commissioned by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III in 1936 as part of his Diamond Jubilee celebrations to perpetuate the memory of his ancestors. Designed by architect V.R. Talwalkar (Talwarkar) with Sir Edward Lutyens's influence, it is an Indo-Saracenic structure on an 'E'-shaped plan near the Vishwamitri Bridge on Kothi Road; the 35-m shikhara is crowned with bronze sun, moon and earth finials and an undivided map of India symbolising national unity. Interiors hold five wall murals by Nandalal Bose (Mahabharata battle, Gangavataran, Life of Meera, Natir Poojan), paintings by Raja Ravi Varma, royal busts, coins and personal items of the Gaekwad rulers; Gupta-era (c. 400 CE) bricks were found during construction. One source describes a sanctum with a shivlinga and an adjoining satsang hall hosting cultural events, so the monument has devotional corners, but its documented identity is a secular memorial museum, not a working temple. CSV row is correctly a memorial record, not a Hindu temple.
